picks.title: Village Halloween Parade
picks.why: Fifty thousand people in costume march up Sixth Avenue, and anyone dressed up can join in. No ticket, no RSVP.

venue.name: Sixth Avenue
venue.address: Lineup at Sixth Ave & Canal St

picks.title: Mariza
picks.why: Mariza is the best-known fado singer of her generation, and Portugal’s music of longing sounds best in a room like McCarter’s.

picks.title: NYC Marathon
picks.why: The best free show in the city: about 50,000 runners, two million people cheering, and First Avenue at its loudest around mile 17.

picks.title: The Haunted Hop
picks.why: New York Night Train’s 21st Halloween soul party: DJ Jonathan Toubin, go-go dancers and Moogstar, the vocoder player from Zapp and Cameo, in a former glass factory.

picks.title: Vince Staples
picks.why: Vince Staples is one of the sharpest, funniest writers in rap, and Franklin Music Hall is the right size for him.

picks.title: Wunderkammer
picks.why: More than twenty taxidermists bring their strangest work to be judged on stage. As odd, and as funny, as it sounds.

picks.title: Cécile McLorin Salvant
picks.why: Three Grammys for best jazz vocal album, and a voice that makes old standards feel newly written.

picks.title: Machine Girl
picks.why: Machine Girl play breakneck digital hardcore that turns any room into a mosh pit, and this is Pioneer Works’ Devil’s Night show.

picks.title: St. Vincent
picks.why: St. Vincent singing standards in the Carlyle’s small supper club, the last of three nights. Bar seats are the cheapest way in.

picks.title: Big Night, and a timpano
picks.why: Watch Big Night, the 1996 film about two brothers and their failing Italian restaurant, then eat the timpano from its famous dinner.

picks.title: Marcel Duchamp
picks.why: The first North American Duchamp retrospective in more than 50 years, at the museum that owns much of his most important work.

people.name: Marcel Duchamp
people.role: French artist; in 1917 he submitted a urinal as a sculpture

picks.title: Día de los Muertos at the Botanical Garden
picks.why: Giant skeleton puppets and monarch butterflies parade through the Garden among marigolds and ofrendas, on the last weekend of the celebration.

picks.title: Neil deGrasse Tyson on meeting aliens
picks.why: Tyson on how we should greet the first aliens we meet, the subject of his new book. Expect jokes and a lot of physics.

people.name: Neil deGrasse Tyson
people.role: Astrophysicist, director of the Hayden Planetarium and host of StarTalk

picks.title: Yiyun Li on her new novel
picks.why: Yiyun Li, one of the most admired novelists teaching at Princeton, on her new book. Free, on campus.

picks.title: Kaiju Big Battel: Satan Sleeps Tonight
picks.why: Grown adults in rubber monster suits wrestle and flatten a cardboard city. A cult show since the 1990s.

picks.title: The Hometown Halloween Parade
picks.why: Princeton’s Halloween parade turns fifty: kids, dogs and whole families in costume around Palmer Square.

picks.title: Robert Glasper
picks.why: Glasper’s fall residency at the Blue Note is a New York tradition, and the late set is where it gets loose.

people.name: Robert Glasper
people.role: Grammy-winning jazz pianist who works with rappers like Kendrick Lamar

picks.title: Afro-Cuban All Stars
picks.why: The Cuban big band led by Juan de Marcos, who helped put together Buena Vista Social Club.

picks.title: The Moth StorySLAM
picks.why: Ten strangers tell true five-minute stories and the audience scores them. Some are great; none are long.

picks.title: Halloween Nights at Eastern State
picks.why: Haunted houses inside a real 1829 prison, in the last stretch of the season.

picks.title: Philosophy at the Cloisters
picks.why: A guided conversation about medieval art inside the Cloisters, the Met’s castle-like branch above the Hudson.

venue.name: The Met Cloisters
venue.address: 99 Margaret Corbin Dr, New York, NY 10040, USA

picks.title: Ólafur Arnalds
picks.why: Quiet piano and strings from the Icelandic composer, in Town Hall’s warm old room.

picks.title: Carillon concert at the Graduate College
picks.why: The Graduate College carillon has 67 bells. The Sunday concerts are free and best heard from the lawn.

venue.name: Princeton University Graduate College, Grover Cleveland Tower

picks.title: Princeton vs. Cornell
picks.why: Ivy League football at Princeton Stadium on Halloween, a short walk from Nassau Street.

picks.title: Boy Harsher
picks.why: Dark, danceable synth music on Halloween night.

picks.title: Jesse Wegman: The Lost Founder
picks.why: A New York Times editorial writer on a founder most people have never heard of. $5 at the Free Library.

people.name: Jesse Wegman
people.role: New York Times editorial board member

picks.title: Brancusi
picks.why: Brancusi’s polished bronzes and the studio he arranged like a work of its own, at MoMA.

picks.title: Day of the Dead in Princeton
picks.why: The Arts Council’s free Day of the Dead celebration, for families, at the Princeton Shopping Center.

picks.title: A walk through Princeton history
picks.why: Two hours on foot through Princeton’s past with the Historical Society, starting at the Battle Monument.

venue.name: Princeton Battle Monument
venue.address: 1 Monument Drive, Princeton, NJ, 08540, United States

picks.title: Joanne McNally
picks.why: Joanne McNally, the Irish comedian behind the podcast My Therapist Ghosted Me, on tour.

picks.title: Organ at noon in the Chapel
picks.why: Half an hour of organ music in the University Chapel, one of the great Gothic rooms in New Jersey. Free, at lunchtime.

picks.title: Paul Moses on The Italian Squad
picks.why: Paul Moses on The Italian Squad, the true story of the immigrant cops who took on the early Mafia in New York.

picks.title: Guerilla Toss
picks.why: Guerilla Toss make wiry, joyful art-punk, and Ruba Club is small enough to stand right at the front.

picks.title: Bass Drum of Death
picks.why: Loud, fast garage punk in Johnny Brenda’s small upstairs room.

places.name: Agricola
places.why: The safe, good choice when parents visit.

places.name: Mistral
places.why: One of downtown Princeton’s better dinners, rated 4.6 by more than 3,000 OpenTable diners.

places.name: XiBei Cuisine
places.why: Opened in 2025. The Daily Princetonian and Princeton Alumni Weekly both recommend it.
places.order: Soup dumplings, beef noodles, tomato and egg noodles.

places.name: Eno Terra
places.why: Rated 4.7 by nearly 4,000 OpenTable diners. Ten minutes from campus.

places.name: Nomad Pizza
places.why: Worth the 15-minute drive from Princeton.

places.name: Jammin’ Crêpes
places.why: Started as a farmers market stand. Featured on Diners, Drive-Ins and Dives.
places.order: Turkey club crêpe, or the 20-layer lemon crêpe cake.

places.name: The Dinky Bar & Kitchen
places.why: Right by McCarter Theatre, so it works before or after a show.

places.name: Hoagie Haven
places.why: The late-night Princeton tradition.

places.name: Mamoun’s Falafel
places.why: The cheap, fast standby downtown. Open 11 am to 9 pm every day.

places.name: The Bent Spoon
places.why: Made with ingredients from New Jersey farms. Worth the walk in any season.

places.name: Kabawa
places.why: Number one on The New York Times’s 2026 list of the city’s 100 best restaurants.

places.name: Semma
places.why: One of the most acclaimed Indian restaurants in the city, and very hard to book.
places.order: Gunpowder dosa, the snail dish (nathai pirattal).

places.name: Torrisi
places.why: Third on The New York Times’s 2026 list of the city’s 100 best restaurants.

places.name: Lei
places.why: Nominated for the 2026 James Beard Best New Restaurant award. About 25 seats and a wine list over 25 pages long.
places.order: Chilled celtuce, cat’s ear noodles, the short rib.

places.name: L’Industrie Pizzeria
places.why: Usually near the top of any New York slice ranking. Expect a line.

places.name: Katz’s Delicatessen
places.why: The classic. Worth it once, and probably again.
places.order: Pastrami on rye. Tip the cutter.

places.name: Thai Diner
places.why: One of the highest-rated restaurants in Manhattan on The Infatuation. Fun, loud and reasonably priced.

places.name: Lucali
places.why: One of the most famous pizzerias in New York.

places.name: Superiority Burger
places.why: A vegetarian restaurant that meat eaters line up for.
places.order: The Superiority Burger, burnt broccoli salad.

places.name: Penny
places.why: Rated 9.4 by The Infatuation. Good for a nice dinner without a full tasting menu.

places.name: Zahav
places.why: Won the James Beard award for Outstanding Restaurant in 2019. Reservations go weeks ahead.
places.order: Pomegranate lamb shoulder for the table.

places.name: Kalaya
places.why: Chef Nok Suntaranon’s restaurant is one of the most celebrated in Philadelphia.

places.name: Emmett
places.why: On The Infatuation’s 25 best restaurants in Philadelphia. Order the tasting menu; à la carte misses a lot.
places.order: The tasting menu. Don’t skip the sesame madeleines.

places.name: Suraya
places.why: One of the best dinners in Fishtown. Sit in the garden when it’s warm.
places.order: Mezze to share, then the kebabs.

places.name: Vernick Food & Drink
places.why: Vernick won the James Beard award for best chef in the Mid-Atlantic. A safe bet for a nice dinner.
places.order: Any of the toasts, the raw bar.

places.name: Pizzeria Beddia
places.why: Bon Appétit named it the best pizza in America in 2015. Still worth the trip.

places.name: John’s Roast Pork
places.why: A family-run shack that won a James Beard America’s Classics award.
places.order: Roast pork with greens and sharp provolone.

places.name: El Chingon
places.why: On The Infatuation’s 25 best restaurants in Philadelphia.
places.order: The clásica cemita with fried chicken, plus aguachile.

places.name: Reading Terminal Market
places.why: The easy answer when a group can’t agree.
places.order: Roast pork at DiNic’s, then a doughnut from Beiler’s.

places.name: Bar Cicci
places.why: On The Infatuation’s Philadelphia Hit List of new restaurants.
